newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa's Mandela to honour Biko 20 years on.
newsitem.headline: South Africa's Mandela to honour Biko 20 years on.

text.p: A statue of South African black consciousness leader Steve Biko will be unveiled by President Nelson Mandela on September 12, the 20th anniversary of his death in detention.
Mandela will also rename a bridge in Biko's honour in the coastal city of East London, Biko's friend Donald Woods said in a statement on Wednesday.
"The Biko family want the event to be inclusive and reconciliatory, in a spirit of national unity," said Woods, a former newspaper editor who first brought Biko's death to the attention of the world.

The bronze statue by South African sculptor Naomi Jacobson is funded by donors including actors Denzel Washington and Kevin Kline as well as Richard Attenborough, who collaborated in the film "Cry, Freedom" based on Biko and his friendship with Woods.
Rock star Peter Gabriel, who recorded the haunting anthem "Biko", British businessman Richard Branson and author Ken Follett also helped back the project, Woods said.

During his life Biko gained prominence as a torchbearer of black consciousness in South Africa, but it was his brutal death in 1977 at the hands of security police inquisitors that made him a world-renowned icon of the anti-apartheid struggle.

The five former security policemen who killed Biko decided in January to come clean on his death, marking one of the biggest successes yet for South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission that is trying to expose human rights abuses under the apartheid era.
The commission has said the men involved are offering to give a full account in return for immunity from prosecution.

Biko's aim of black majority rule was achieved in April 1994, when Mandela's government took power. One of its priorities was setting up the truth commission, mandated to heal the wounds of apartheid through confession and catharsis.
